rows.subtype: Approach: uses good enough for low-stakes decisions to save mental energy [Thinking]
rows.description: A hostel student chooses a laptop bag by two criteria, price under a limit and a padded pocket, and stops. Saving hours of comparison leaves time for exam preparation.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.subtype: Approach: sets the bar too low on an important decision [Pitfall]
rows.description: A young professional accepts the first flat that meets basic needs but skips checking the lease terms and the commute. The threshold fit a cheap purchase and did not fit a year-long commitment.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.subtype: Approach: raises the threshold after noticing the stakes and rechecks options [Revision]
rows.description: Realising a rental is a big commitment, she adds criteria such as noise, water supply and landlord reputation, and visits two more flats before deciding.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.subtype: Approach: scores options against weighted criteria in a table [Thinking]
rows.description: A student picking a stream after Class 10 lists interest, job outlook, effort and distance of college. He weights them, scores each stream and compares the totals.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 18–22, 23–26

rows.subtype: Approach: builds the matrix in a spreadsheet and adjusts weights to see how the ranking changes [Action]
rows.description: A student comparing three job offers puts salary, learning, location and growth in columns, then changes weights to test whether the winner holds up.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 23–26

rows.subtype: Approach: fudges scores to make the matrix confirm a favourite [Pitfall]
rows.description: A student who already loves one college gives it high scores on subjective criteria and low scores on rivals. The tidy numbers look objective but hide a decision made beforehand.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 23–26

rows.subtype: Approach: uses the matrix to expose which criterion truly drives a choice [Thinking]
rows.description: A young couple comparing flats notices that whichever weights they use, commute time decides the outcome, which shows them what they actually care about.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22

rows.subtype: Approach: notices a gut feeling against the top score and revisits the criteria [Revision]
rows.description: When a matrix favours a job she dreads, she asks what is missing, adds team culture and daily work as criteria, and the ranking changes.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22

rows.subtype: Approach: solves a new problem by comparing it with a familiar one [Thinking]
rows.description: A child who cannot open a new jar remembers that her mother twists the lid of the pickle jar, and she copies that turning motion.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.subtype: Approach: uses an earlier solved problem as a model for a new one [Action]
rows.description: A boy asked to share cricket turns among five friends recalls how the class used a roll-number order for the library, and sets up a rotating list.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
